title: CelluWeave B：湿态压缩条件与测量时点
researchQuestion: Evaluation of the compressive modulus and shape retention of a hydrogel formulation consisting of sodium alginate and cellulose.
mainFindings: The average compressive modulus of the material is 48.0 kPa.
The shape retention rate of the material is 94%.
The average compressive modulus is 48.0 kPa with a sample standard deviation of 3.0 kPa (n=6).
methods: Preparation of a formulation with 2.0% (w/v) sodium alginate and 0.8% (w/v) cellulose
Crosslinking using 50 mmol/L calcium chloride for 10 minutes
Equilibration in a wet state for 1 hour
Measurement of compressive modulus at 15% strain
methodsSummary: The study utilized a hydrogel composed of 2.0% (w/v) sodium alginate and 0.8% (w/v) cellulose, cured with 50 mmol/L calcium chloride for 10 minutes. After 1 hour of wet state equilibrium, the compressive modulus was measured at 15% strain.
importantResults: The average compressive modulus is 48.0 kPa with a sample standard deviation of 3.0 kPa (n=6).

limitations: Differences in strain (15% vs 10%) and equilibrium duration (1 hour vs 24 hours) compared to P17 prevent assertions of superior material performance
Water absorption rate, cell viability, and cost were not reported
shortSummary: This study reports that a hydrogel formulation of 2.0% sodium alginate and 0.8% cellulose, crosslinked with 50 mmol/L calcium chloride, exhibits an average compressive modulus of 48.0 kPa at 15% strain and a shape retention rate of 94%.
